extra.reason: Added context config field, threaded through prompt + cache-busting
Added status='unhoarded' + note column, mark_unhoarded() in state.py, and --unhoarded/--note flags in cmd_mark. stats breaks it out automatically via status grouping.

Added WritebackAdapter protocol (base.py), RaindropAdapter.mark_unhoarded() that merges the configurable tag into existing tags and optionally moves to a collection, plus config fields (unhoarded_tag, unhoarded_collection_id) wired through sources.py. Verified with a mocked HTTP session -- no live API calls made.

Added find_adapter_for_source() in sources.py and wired it into cmd_mark's --unhoarded path in cli.py. Write-back is best-effort: no adapter match or an exception both degrade to a stderr warning while the local state change (source of truth) still succeeds. Verified all three paths (write-back success, no-support source, write-back failure) with mocked/patched adapters -- no live Raindrop API calls made.

Revised the read-only claim, added a 'What Unhoarded Means' section explaining the done vs. unhoarded distinction and write-back behavior, added --unhoarded example to Daily Use, and documented unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id in Config Reference.
All four child issues complete: local unhoarded state + note field, WritebackAdapter protocol + Raindrop tag/collection implementation, CLI wiring with best-effort write-back, and README docs.
Extended cmd_init's next-steps to point at config.toml's commented-out context and unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id examples instead of staying silent about them.

Added RaindropAdapter.apply_updates() (generalized partial update: tags merge, collection move, note set -- any subset) and list_collections() (flattens top-level + nested via /collections and /collections/childrens). mark_unhoarded() is now a thin wrapper over apply_updates(). Extended WritebackAdapter protocol in base.py to match. Verified with mocked HTTP sessions: regression on mark_unhoarded, tags-only/note-only/no-op apply_updates paths, and collection listing -- no live API calls.

Extended PROMPT_TEMPLATE to ask for Tags/Collection lines grounded in the real Raindrop collection list (fetched once per digest run, only when at least one stale item actually needs fresh summarization). Added parse_summary_response() to structure the AI reply instead of treating it as an opaque blob. New suggested_tags/suggested_collection columns in state.py. digest.py stores a clean Summary+Action body (no duplication) plus a separate suggestion line pointing at the future 'unhoard apply' command. Verified: parser edge cases, full digest flow with mocked Anthropic+Raindrop calls, zero-network-call re-run on fully cached items, and the no-Raindrop-adapter fallback (chrome items still get Summary/Action, no collection grounding).

Added 'unhoard apply <key> [--tags] [--collection] [--summary] [--all]'. Resolves suggested tags/collection from local state, matches collection name to id via list_collections() (case-insensitive, skips gracefully if the collection no longer exists), writes the AI summary as a note. Best-effort like mark --unhoarded: no write-back support or a failed API call both exit cleanly with a message. Added mark_applied() tracking (tags_applied_at/collection_applied_at/summary_applied_at) so the digest stops suggesting things already pushed -- resolves the open design question in favor of tracking. Factored the repeated 'find item by key' logic out of cmd_mark into _find_single_item(), reused by cmd_apply. Verified: happy path, no-suggestions warning, stale/deleted collection name, no-write-back source, unknown key, and the digest suppression of already-applied suggestions -- all via mocked adapters, no live API calls.

Documented 'unhoard apply' in Daily Use, added a 'Suggested Tags & Collection' section explaining grounding, the apply flags, applied-state tracking, and the shared-note-field last-write-wins behavior with mark --unhoarded --note.

All four child issues complete: Raindrop adapter capabilities (list_collections + generalized apply_updates), AI prompt/parsing extension for grounded tag/collection suggestions, the 'unhoard apply' command with applied-state tracking, and docs.

Added rich and questionary as dependencies (uv add rich questionary -- resolved cleanly, questionary had no prompt_toolkit conflicts unlike PyInquirer would have). New unhoard/ui.py with a shared Console (stdout) + err_console (stderr) and print_success/print_warning/print_error helpers. No command output migrated yet -- that's e5b.2. Verified rich correctly auto-detects non-TTY output and strips ANSI codes when piped, and that questionary imports cleanly. Existing CLI behavior unaffected.

Migrated init/sync/mark/apply/stats to ui.py's Console/print_success/print_warning/print_error. init's next-steps now render in a rich Panel; stats renders as two rich Tables (by status, active-by-source) instead of manual print lines. Escaped all dynamic content (item titles, error messages, source names, collection titles, tags, config paths) via rich.markup.escape() since titles/collections come from arbitrary web content and Raindrop collections that can contain literal brackets -- verified this explicitly with a bracket/angle-bracket-laden title through mark and apply, nothing broke. digest.py/cmd_digest untouched (that's e5b.3). Verified piped/non-TTY output (stats | cat) degrades to plain box-drawing text with no raw ANSI codes, same exit codes and information as before throughout.

digest --print now renders through rich.markdown.Markdown instead of dumping raw source; saved digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md files are unaffected (same build_digest() output, just rendered differently at print time). Added a rich.progress bar around the stale-item loop, gated by the same needs_fresh check that already controls collection-name fetching -- no bar shown on a fully-cached digest.

Along the way, fixed a real markdown-structure bug this surfaced: <sub> tags and lazy blockquote continuation (no '>' prefix on the Action line) were causing Summary/Action/suggestion/key to merge into one garbled paragraph under any real CommonMark renderer -- previously invisible because --print just dumped raw markdown source. Restructured each stale/aging/new item into properly blank-line-separated blocks (bullet header, blockquote, suggestion line, key line, each as *emphasis* instead of raw <sub> HTML) and collapsed Summary+Action onto one line to avoid blockquote soft-break ambiguity. This fixes both the new --print rendering and the previously-broken structure of the saved .md files themselves. Verified: rendered output structure, raw saved file structure, piped/non-TTY --print (clean degradation, single-line progress bar summary, no ANSI codes), and full command regression.

Added _is_interactive() (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()) gate in _find_single_item(). When both are true and there's an ambiguous match, uses questionary.select() to let the user pick interactively; a cancelled picker (Ctrl-C/Esc, .ask() returns None) is treated the same as no match. Non-interactive contexts (cron, scripts, piped, and this sandboxed environment itself) keep the exact old behavior: print the list, return None, exit 1 -- verified against a real subprocess with no attached tty, plus mocked-isatty tests for the select/cancel/unambiguous-skips-picker paths. Full command regression unaffected.

Added a 'CLI Experience' section covering rich-formatted output, digest --print Markdown rendering (saved files unaffected), the progress bar's fully-cached-skips-it behavior, and the questionary interactive picker's TTY-only gating. Also fixed the now-outdated <sub> example in the existing 'Suggested Tags & Collection' section to match the *emphasis* markup from e5b.3.

All five child issues complete: rich + questionary dependencies with a shared ui.py module, rich-formatted sync/mark/apply/stats/init output, digest --print rendered as Markdown with a progress bar (plus a real markdown-structure bug fix this surfaced), a TTY-gated interactive picker for ambiguous key matches via questionary, and docs.

Dropped required=True from the subparsers and added an explicit args.command is None check in main() that prints the full parser help (via format_help(), escaped and routed through the shared rich Console for consistency) and returns 1, instead of argparse's bare 'error: the following arguments are required' message. --help and actual invalid-command errors are unaffected.

Added 'unhoard synthesize <key> [--force]'. Fetches full article text via summarize.py's existing fetch_article_text() (same trafilatura path already used for AI summaries) and writes a standalone note to <output_dir>/synthesized/<slug>.md with YAML frontmatter (title/url/source/key/tags/synthesized_at) plus a Summary section (if a cached AI summary exists) and the full text. Frontmatter strings/arrays are built with json.dumps(), which produces valid YAML flow scalars/sequences -- verified round-tripping a title with brackets, colons, and quotes through a real YAML parser. Won't overwrite an existing note unless --force is passed (real file-existence check, not just the new synthesized_at DB column, which is informational only). Empty/unfetchable article text fails cleanly with exit 1 instead of writing a useless note. Distinct from mark --unhoarded, which stays a separate, later step.
